items.title: Anthropic publishes agent memory components, including offline dreaming consolidation
items.summary: Anthropic's engineering blog describes how Claude agent memory is organized and how an offline dreaming pass consolidates notes, corrects mistakes against transcripts, and promotes useful items for later retrieval. Builders get a concrete write-up of memory hierarchy and maintenance rather than a new public API.

doubt.pushback: Some replies call dreaming peak product marketing for an overnight batch memory compaction job.

reception.summary: Many welcome memory consolidation for agents; critics say the dreaming label oversells a maintenance pass and ask who pays for the compute.

items.title: Nous Research releases Arete-27B: Qwen3.8-27B post-trained against China-aligned propaganda
items.summary: Arete-27B fine-tunes Qwen3.8-27B on about 53M tokens so an 803-prompt propaganda eval falls from 22% to 1% without a clear Hermes Bench drop. Weights, eval, training data, and blog are public for teams that want open Chinese bases with Western value behavior.

doubt.pushback: Some quote posters treat western values as a political dog whistle rather than a measured eval target.

reception.summary: Most quotes praise open-weight value steering and security usefulness; a minority jokes about politics or questions the framing.

items.title: Claude Code cloud sessions auto-detect deps and save environments on Pro, Max, Ultra
items.summary: Claude Code cloud sessions on Pro, Max, and Ultra now infer dependencies, network access, and needed API keys, then persist the environment for the next run. Keys are stored so the model does not see them, cutting repeated setup for cloud agent loops.

doubt.pushback: A few quotes say the feature copies earlier ADE/T3 Code environment work rather than inventing it.

reception.summary: Developers welcome less cloud setup friction; some note feature overlap with other agent IDEs and one older User-Agent email header complaint unrelated to this change.

items.title: GitHub's new Git storage handles 5,000 concurrent agents at 7,200 pushes/sec in tests
items.summary: GitHub says a new Git storage architecture supported 5,000 concurrent agents on one repo at 7,200 pushes per second in internal tests while keeping read latency low. That matters for teams running many coding agents against the same repository.

doubt.pushback: Numbers are internal tests only; no public method or independent reproduction yet.

items.title: Together Compiler: agents continually re-optimize inference kernels per model and traffic
items.summary: Together AI launched Together Compiler, agents that keep optimizing kernels for a customer's model, hardware, and traffic. They report +12% to +20% median TPS on already hand-tuned serverless endpoints and roughly one-third to one-half lower response times in production.

doubt.pushback: Vendor-reported speedups on Together's own stack; no third-party benchmark yet.

items.title: NVIDIA Lyra 2.0 turns one image into an explorable generative 3D world
items.summary: Lyra 2.0 combines video generation with 3D reconstruction so a single image becomes a camera-path world that stays more consistent as you revisit places. Paper, Lyra-2 code, and NVIDIA Lyra-2.0 weights/demos are linked for researchers and builders.

items.title: RoboSpoof: video tampering pushes embodied frontier models into harmful robot actions
items.summary: Robocurve shows perceptual attacks (blur or doctored camera feeds) raise harmful attempt rates across frontier embodied models, including 100% attempts on some RoboHarm-style tasks. PDF and blog are up for CoRL Late Breaking Results.

items.title: Frontier Model Forum ships jailbreak rating framework for frontier cyber threats
items.summary: OpenAI and Frontier Model Forum member firms published a shared framework for rating when cyber jailbreaks unlock serious harm and how readily they can be used. It is a common methodology for comparing safeguard bypass severity across frontier systems.

doubt.pushback: Policy-adjacent announcement; usefulness depends on whether labs actually share comparable ratings.

items.title: Cooldown plugin for Hermes Agent blocks OSV malware and asks before installing fresh packages
items.summary: Cooldown is a Hermes Agent plugin that checks packages before install: it blocks OSV-listed malware and prompts the user when a release is under three days old. Repo is public for fleets that let coding agents install dependencies.

doubt.pushback: Early hackathon plugin; small engagement and no independent audit cited.

items.title: DataLab API submits and result checks are about 2x faster; SDK 0.9.1 lands
items.summary: DataLab cut median document submit latency from 670 ms to 314 ms and result checks from 128 ms to 62 ms, with Python SDK 0.9.1 picking up finished results sooner. Useful for document parsing pipelines that poll their API.

items.title: Muir: linear attention with sensitivity-allocated gating and matched-filter readout
items.summary: The Muir paper proposes linear attention that allocates gating by sensitivity and uses a matched-filter readout. The Hugging Face Papers card is the primary link for researchers tracking efficient attention variants.

doubt.pushback: Paper card only so far; no independent reproduction called out in-thread.

items.title: Gemini Live API schema adds proactive video that reacts to camera frames unprompted
items.summary: A tracker notes a Gemini Live API schema option for proactive video so the model can react to incoming camera frames without a user prompt, requiring proactive audio and warning of higher cost. Not documented on the public docs page yet.

doubt.pushback: Leak-tracker claim only; no official docs or Google announcement in this window.
